name: fighter-auto

webgpu.note: the same dual cart on romdev and Chromium against native WebGPU; GL vs WebGPU within 25 percent of pixels (particles, dust, shockwave)

note: Fighter: two computer fighters (Bolt and Vex, rooftop) play from the intro with the punch / kick / block controls (the computer blocks with the block button, guards low against lows, parries now and then). The rules are integer only (sim.c), so the named state must match exactly on every host; the expects pin this run. The control is one frame short. Repinned for F-PT3 (2026-10-29): the computer plays through the same input rules as a pad, and the new movement changes its fight: its down presses now crouch, its jump-in is one up-forward press (it was two up taps), held directions it sends walk or jump where they stood still. Before [598,823] hp, stats [11,3,3,0,0,1]; after [541,590], [19,0,0,0,3,0] in these 900 frames. The 24-match soak is close to before (blocks 221 to 205, parries 81 to 66, throws 23 to 17, median round 28.1 to 25.6 s).

name: fighter-p1-moves

webgpu.note: dual cart on romdev and Chromium against native WebGPU, and on romdev GL against native GL

note: Player 1 on a pad plays the new controls against a standing player 2: down, down-forward, forward + punch (a fireball), walk in, up + punch (a high punch), down + kick (a sweep), punch into kick (a chain), punch + kick (a throw). The control leaves the fireball motion out. Expects: 4 hits and 1 throw (sim.stats), 270 damage, the same state hash on every host.

name: fighter-guard

webgpu.note: dual cart on romdev and Chromium against native WebGPU, and on romdev GL against native GL

note: The guard triangle with pads: player 2 holds down + block (a low guard) while player 1 does up + kick (a high: it passes over, sim.stats[4] counts it ducked), down + punch and kick (one is blocked low, sim.stats[1]); then player 2 lets go and the kick lands (one hit, 60 damage). Expects: stats [hits 1, blocks 1, parries 0, guard breaks 0, ducked 1, throws 0]. The control: player 2 never guards (2 hits, nothing blocked or ducked).

name: fighter-dpad-walk

webgpu.note: dual cart on romdev and Chromium against native WebGPU, and on romdev GL against native GL

note: F-PT3 "holding a direction does nothing": the d-pad held right 2 s and left 1 s, rolling onto up-right / down-right (up-left / down-left) for 2 to 4 frames now and then. Expect: walking on all 180 held frames, no jump, crouch or dash. On the old build (main 8612ca7) the same script walks 48 of 180 frames and dashes 4 times (a roll 6 9 6 read as a double tap). Control: the rolls held 9 frames (3 jumps, the walk breaks). ctl.p1 is player 1: [walk frames, takeoffs, forward takeoffs, back takeoffs, high normals, low normals, crouch frames, dashes, highest jump mm, jump attacks].

name: fighter-dpad-jumps

note: F-PT3 "jumping inconsistent": single up taps of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 frames on the d-pad (6 jumps, every one 1207 mm high), up-forward and up-back pressed directly and rolled into from up or from a walk back (a 4-frame roll from a walk stays a walk, the drift rule; 9 frames jumps), up + punch on the same frame, punch 2 frames after up and 2 frames before up, up + kick (4 high normals, no jump), a held down (40 crouch frames), down + kick (the sweep), fast forward / back alternation (no dash). name: fighter-rumble

webgpu.note: dual cart on romdev and Chromium against native WebGPU, and on romdev GL against native GL

note: No shake: player 1 lands 4 hits and a throw on player 2 (the fighter-p1-moves script) while the camera as drawn is held against the framing on every frame within half a second of an impact (cam.offset: 137 frames, none off by over 0.1 mm or 0.1 milliradian; the build before: all 137 off, up to 13 cm and radians summed). The hits are felt in the pads instead: rumble.sent counts the requests to player 1 (dealt) and player 2 (taken), cw.rumble is the engine's last (pad 1). The sim hash is the one fighter-p1-moves pins: the shake was never in the rules. Control: the script without the fireball.
